body:
Yesterday a plan lay on the table. Today the refusal lies beside it. Between the two, in New York, two men shake hands who have not sat together in four years, and in Paris a square fills that once belonged to the Revolution.

I. Eight points, one refusal

Beijing tallies the visit in eight points: tariff cuts of thirty billion dollars on unsensitive goods, a trade council, a channel for incidents involving artificial intelligence. Next round in November; APEC in Shenzhen, the G20 in Miami. The two thrones have drawn closer without exchanging blades. 1 2

Trump rejects the seven-day plan in front of the White House. He remains willing to talk, not on these terms. The tankers wait longer than the diplomats. 5 6

II. Twenty minutes

Johann Wadephul and Sergey Lavrov sit at one table. Barely twenty minutes. A handshake. The hall stays bright, and so does the cold. Trump publicly tells Zelenskyy to come to terms with Putin. 3 7

III. The square that fills

In Paris, seven to eight hundred thousand people stand on the Place de la Concorde. Leo XIV speaks of machines that must serve the human being, not dominion. Then Lourdes. 8

IV. At the edge of the page

While the cards lie in New York and Paris, Saturday writes elsewhere. In Dera Ismail Khan a bomber kills twelve at a police post and wounds thirty. Bangkok declares a flood disaster; at least two dead, tens of thousands affected. A nor'easter on the American East Coast cancels four hundred flights, cuts power to sixty-eight thousand homes and kills one person in New York. Off Kamchatka the fishing vessel Triumf burns. In Gauteng gunmen kill tavern guests — seventeen in Carletonville; other counts speak of two massacres and more than twenty dead. Gaza's health ministry puts the war's death toll above seventy-four thousand. 9 10

The chronicler's close

Three cards lie open in the great halls. At the edge of the page lie those who make no speech. Whether Tehran lays down a new hand belongs to the next leaf.
